blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 25 in June to 32 in October (+28.0%), and it took 1.1% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 7 in June to 3 in October (−57.1%), and it took 0.5% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Bridgeview for detached houses in August (a sellers’ best bet).

items.t: Bridgeview has no City-published boundary of its own; the City of Surrey calls it a historic neighbourhood in Whalley, anchored by Bridgeview Park at 12560 115 Avenue. The City describes the park as located in the historic neighbourhood of Bridgeview.

The plan area beside it is South Westminster, bordered by the Fraser River in the west, King George Boulevard in the north and 96 Avenue in the south, and described by the City as the largely industrial area along the river between Scott Road SkyTrain Station and the Surrey Fraser Docks (Port of Vancouver).

Uphill to the east sits South Westminster Heights, about 30.86 hectares bounded by Old Yale Road (north), 128 Street (east), 104 Avenue (south) and 125B Street (west) — a separate infill plan area, not part of the riverfront lowland.

The residential stock is an older lowland neighbourhood beside industrial land, not a planned new subdivision. The City's industrial overview states Bridgeview is predominantly zoned for residential and industrial uses, with a mix of light industrial, commercial and residential zones.

The adjoining South Westminster Heights area is described by the City as a more traditional single-family area with older lots and mature trees, which is the character of the streets rising east of the lowland.
Bridgeview Park at 12560 115 Avenue carries the outdoor stock: playground, water park, picnic shelters, two softball diamonds, a multi-use field, and tennis, pickleball and basketball courts.

The South Westminster Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP), approved in December 2003, is the plan that governs the riverfront side, and its update was endorsed on March 10, 2025. The 2025 update concluded the Stage 2 land use for the mainly industrial portion and named a Transit Village Study Area at Scott Road Station and a Waterfront District Study Area.

Flood building rules apply on the lowland lots: the City's Bridgeview Floodplain guide requires a geotechnical engineer for construction in the floodplain, sets a Flood Construction Level (FCL), and allows no habitable area below the FCL, enforced by a restrictive covenant on title.

One in-area application shows the elevation rule in numbers: a City planning report for 11444–124 Street states the site is within the Fraser River floodplain and requires a Minimum Building Elevation of 4.8 metres geodetic.

blocks.text: Bridgeview: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The river beach is Brownsville Bar Park, 11931 Old Yale Road, one of the only Fraser River locations with a sandy beach and about 300 metres of waterfront, sitting between the Pattullo and SkyTrain bridges at the end of the Tannery Greenway.

The old crossing here is a registered heritage site: Brownsville Park and Sandbar, City heritage Site No. 223 in the 1100 block of Portage Road, registered January 12, 2004, marking the early Brownsville ferry landing at the foot of Old Yale Road.
There is no Surrey Libraries branch inside Bridgeview; the City system lists ten branches city-wide, and the Whalley-area branch is City Centre at 10350 University Drive.

Soil is a lot-level check here: the City floodplain guide flags methane gas from decomposing organic soils common to Bridgeview, which is why a geotechnical report is required for floodplain construction.
The community centre's hours are part-time, not full-week: programs only on Monday and Friday, with public hours on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evenings and weekend days.

The Pattullo Bridge Replacement is the area-defining project, and its replacement bridge is now open. The project's July 2026 monthly status report states the stal̕əw̓asəm (Riverview) Bridge, which replaces the Pattullo Bridge, opened one northbound lane in December 2025 and all four lanes in February 2026, the Pattullo Bridge is now closed, and deconstruction is underway; Transportation Investment Corporation (TI Corp) oversees the $1.637 billion project. Status: bridge open, old bridge deconstruction underway (as of November 3, 2026).

South Westminster Transit Village and Waterfront District, Scott Road Station area: the City states Council endorsed the updated plan on March 10, 2025, granting Stage 1 land use for a Transit Village of housing and retail at the station and identifying a Waterfront District Study Area for a feasibility study. Status: study stage (as of November 3, 2026).

Temporary Use Permit application 7924-0145-00, 11444 and 11426 124 Street (sites at 11456 and 11462 124 Street), for a truck park and outdoor lumber storage on a 1.6-hectare site zoned Special Industry (I-4): the November 17, 2025 planning report recommended the permit proceed to public notification. Status: application in process (as of November 3, 2026).

The Bridgeview-specific charge is the area Development Cost Charge (DCC) schedule: the City publishes separate 2025 Bridgeview / South Westminster DCC rates, including an industrial total of $108,406 per acre and a commercial rate of $14.58 per square foot of building area (excluding several commercial zones), so a rebuild or new project here is costed under that schedule.

No SkyTrain station sits inside the residential streets; Scott Road Station on the Expo Line is the area's rapid-transit anchor, named by the City as the station the South Westminster plan is built around.

The in-neighbourhood bus is route 371, Surrey Central Station to Scott Road Station, which TransLink's timetable routes through Bridgeview on Bridgeview Drive, 115 Avenue, 128 Street, 132 Street, 114 Avenue and 112 Avenue.

The R6 Scott Road RapidBus launched January 2, 2024, runs between Scott Road Station and Newton Exchange from 5 a.m. to 1 a.m. daily, with 15-minute-or-better service all day, and route 319 continues alongside it serving local stops.

Flood is the first check: the City states Surrey's Fraser River floodplain covers 776 hectares of developed land with a mix of industrial and residential properties, protected by dykes, concrete flood walls and four pump stations that drain land behind the dykes during tides, storm surge and freshet.

Look a specific lot up in the City's Bridgeview Floodplain guide and COSMOS mapping before buying: the guide sets the lot's Flood Construction Level and covenant position, and states lots from a recent subdivision can carry minimum building elevations set by that subdivision's engineer, which the guide itself does not list.
The South Westminster shore is described by the City as a very low flood bench that flooded in 1972, so an older house's as-built elevation is a document to ask for, not an assumption.

faq.q: Is Bridgeview its own plan area, or part of somewhere else?
faq.a: It has no plan of its own. A buyer's lot can sit in either frame, so check which plan the address falls under.

Bridgeview Elementary, Kindergarten to Grade 7, at 12834 115A Avenue is the in-area school. The provincial school list for School District 36 (Surrey) gives that address and grade range, and lists Kwantlen Park Secondary, Grades 8–12, at 10441 132 Street. Catchments are address-based, so confirm the exact house address in the district school locator before an offer that depends on a school.

faq.q: Can I use the basement as a suite or bedroom?
faq.a: Not below the flood construction level. The City's Bridgeview Floodplain guide states habitable area is not permitted below the FCL and that a restrictive covenant on title enforces the ban, so a low basement in the floodplain is storage or utility space, not living space, even if a previous owner finished it.

faq.q: Will the land beside the houses stay industrial?
faq.a: Mostly, with two exceptions now in study. The March 2025 South Westminster update kept Mixed Employment and Industrial designations for the Stage 2 lands, while naming a Transit Village of housing and retail at Scott Road Station and a Waterfront District feasibility study — both study areas, not adopted residential designations yet.
